complete circuit
A loop with no gaps, so current can flow all the way round.
volt
The unit of voltage. More volts means a bigger push.
circuit symbol
A simple drawing that stands for a part of a circuit. Scientists everywhere use the same symbols.
independent variable
The one thing you change in a fair test.
dependent variable
The thing you measure in a fair test.
controlled variable
Something you keep the same in a fair test.
induction
Making a voltage in a wire by moving a magnet near it.
energy transfer
Energy moving from one form to another, such as electrical energy to light and heat.
useful energy
The energy that does the job we want, such as light from a lamp.
wasted energy
Energy that doesn’t do the job we want. It is often heat that spreads into the surroundings.
hertz
The unit of frequency. 1 Hz means one complete cycle every second.
oscilloscope
A screen that draws a graph of voltage as time goes on, so you can see how electricity changes.
mains
The electricity that comes to the sockets in our walls. In Beijing it is 220 V AC at 50 Hz.
